title: Recover from per-iteration HEAD divergence in change persister + drop hand-bumped health version literal (revised)
summary: Replace the bare `raise RuntimeError(...)` in the divergence branch of `adapters/git_change_persister.py` with `_recover_from_divergence(...)` that (1) pushes the divergent HEAD to `{branch}-backup-{prefix}` on the configured remote BEFORE any state mutation, (2) captures `head_tree` + `head_message_divergent` before reset, (3) `reset --hard`s the worktree to `origin/{branch}` (one reset moves the shared `refs/heads/{branch}` ref per `git worktree` docs), (4) on tree-equal: reads the remote-tip's message AFTER reset so `PersistResult.message` describes `commit_sha = remote_tip` correctly (fixing the invariant violation in the prior draft), (5) on tree-differ: synthesizes one replay commit via `git commit-tree` whose parent IS the remote tip and pushes fast-forward — no `--force` anywhere. Plumbing: extend `GitService` Protocol AND `ChangePersister` Protocol (the prior draft missed the latter); implement three new methods in `SubprocessGitService` and extract `_author_env` to deduplicate the `GIT_AUTHOR_*` dict between `commit` and `commit_tree`; extend `FakeGitService` AND `FakeChangePersister.persist` signature; add `DIVERGENCE_REPLAY` to `PersistSource`; add required kwarg `backup_ref_id_prefix: str` to `persist(...)` (semantically honest rename — `session_id_prefix` would be a lie because `session_id` is always None in the workflow path per `ralph_loop.py:115-117`); `agent_service` computes `(session_id or generate_job_id())[:8]` using the DOMAIN helper (not stdlib `uuid`). All four prior call sites in `tests/adapters/test_git_change_persister.py` and one in `tests/integration/test_workflow_e2e.py` are updated; `test_persist_raises_on_diverged_head` (which would now fail) is rewritten into three FakeGitService-driven recovery tests; the parametrized integration test is rewritten to assert recovery succeeds against both `origin` and `upstream`. Unrelated cleanup: `src/kodezart/domain/health.py` replaces `_APP_VERSION = "0.1.0"` with `_APP_VERSION = version("kodezart")` from `importlib.metadata`. No `try/except PackageNotFoundError` fallback (per project's no-fallback rule); the existing `make test` → `uv run pytest` flow auto-syncs and installs the project as editable, satisfying dist-info resolution. CONTRIBUTING.md gains a single bullet documenting the install precondition for raw-`pytest` invocations. Both the persister module docstring (lines 1-11) and the `persist` method docstring (lines 51-60) are replaced with pinned exact text reflecting the new three-path decision tree. `pyproject.toml` and `check_health()` are untouched.
context:
## Why this revision

Reviewer rejected the previous draft for four converging reasons; this revision addresses every one.

**(1) Existing divergence-raising tests omitted.** `tests/adapters/test_git_change_persister.py:144-172` (`test_persist_raises_on_diverged_head`) and the parametrized integration test `tests/integration/test_workflow_e2e.py:718-787` (`test_git_change_persister_divergence_error_references_configured_remote`) both assert `pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="diverged")` on the exact path the new recovery handles. Both must be rewritten in this PR — not deferred. The integration parametrize over `["origin", "upstream"]` is preserved (it still verifies the persister honors the configured remote name end-to-end); the assertion target shifts from "RuntimeError references remote/main" to "PersistResult.source is DIVERGENCE_REPLAY, backup ref exists on bare remote under the configured remote name, and remote tip of main is the replay SHA."

**(2) Protocol + FakeChangePersister inconsistency.** The prior draft added `backup_ref_id_prefix` (formerly `session_id_prefix`) to the adapter's `persist(...)` but not to the `ChangePersister` Protocol in `core/protocols.py:188-200` nor to `FakeChangePersister.persist` in `tests/fakes.py:443-456`. The Protocol is the cross-boundary contract; both port and fake must match the adapter. Additionally, the four direct `persister.persist(...)` call sites in `tests/adapters/test_git_change_persister.py` (lines 76-80, 130-134, 168-172, 181-185) and the one at `tests/integration/test_workflow_e2e.py:773` all require the new kwarg — three are still relevant (the divergence-raise tests will be rewritten in place).

**(3) `PersistResult.message` invariant violation on the tree-equal branch.** The prior draft returned `PersistResult(commit_sha=remote_tip, message=head_message)` where `head_message` was captured from the divergent HEAD's commit — describing a DIFFERENT commit than `commit_sha`. The fix: read `head_commit_message(workspace_path)` AFTER `reset_hard(remote_tip)` (HEAD is now at remote_tip, so the read returns remote_tip's message). The tree-differ branch's message is unchanged — `head_message_divergent` IS the replay commit's message because we pass it to `commit_tree`.

**(4) `PackageNotFoundError` risk under `pytest`.** `pyproject.toml:80` configures `pythonpath=["src"]` which only enables imports; it does NOT install dist-info. `importlib.metadata.version("kodezart")` at module import needs the wheel installed. Verified via uv docs: `uv run pytest` (what `make test` runs) auto-syncs and installs the project as editable, so `version("kodezart")` resolves under the standard `make test`/`make check` flow. The remaining risk applies only to a developer running `pytest` directly without `uv run` — a convention issue. Per the project's no-fallback rule, the fix is documentation (CONTRIBUTING.md bullet), NOT a `try/except` fallback.

## Reviewer-driven cleanups folded in

- **`if remote_tip is None: raise` instead of `assert`.** `assert` is stripped under `-O` and is not a production guard. `if/raise` narrows for mypy strict identically.
- **Extract `_author_env(name, email) -> dict[str, str]`** as a static helper on `SubprocessGitService` to share the `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` dict between `commit` (lines 144-149) and the new `commit_tree`.
- **Use `generate_job_id()` from `kodezart.domain.agent`** in `agent_service` for the prefix fallback (NOT `uuid.uuid4().hex`). Services depend on the domain layer for ID generation per the project's layering rules (`README.md:184-188`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:74-87`).
- **Rename kwarg** `session_id_prefix → backup_ref_id_prefix`. `session_id` is always None at the workflow-path call site (`ralph_loop.py:115-117` comment: "Session_id capture is NOT needed here"), so naming it `session_id_prefix` would be a semantic lie.
- **Soften the `importlib.metadata` no-I/O claim.** Per `docs.python.org`, `version()` has no API-guaranteed per-call caching (there IS mtime-based FastPath caching internally, but it's not promised). The module-level assignment to `_APP_VERSION` is what mitigates per-request cost; `check_health()`'s body remains a pure attribute read.
- **Document the backup-push reachability invariant.** Backup-push-first preserves the divergent commit object on the remote (and therefore its tree), keeping `tree_of(head_sha)` independent of local GC timing. We ALSO defensively capture `head_tree` before `reset_hard` so the recovery is correct even if a worktree were to aggressively prune (it doesn't, but the belt-and-suspenders codifies the invariant).
- **Broaden docstring updates AND pin exact replacement text.** The prior draft said "update" without supplying the new text — leaves it to implementer interpretation. The module docstring (lines 1-11) and the `persist` method docstring (lines 51-60) get pinned exact replacements describing the new three-path decision tree.
- **Pin the helper signature** so the implementation cannot drift: `async def _recover_from_divergence(self, *, workspace_path: str, branch: str, head_sha: str, remote_tip: str, backup_ref_id_prefix: str) -> PersistResult`.
- **Enumerate structured-log events** in the change-list: `divergence_backup_push_failed`, `divergence_recovered_tree_equal`, `divergence_recovered_replay`.

## Why keep the kwarg at all (vs the reviewer's YAGNI suggestion)

The reviewer's YAGNI argument is real: `session_id` is always None at the persist call site in the production workflow path, so the fallback always fires and the persister could mint its own prefix. However, the ticket's explicit success signals require: "The backup ref name is produced via `BackupBranchName` with an 8-char prefix sourced from `session_id[:8]`" AND "`services/agent_service.py` passes the `session_id`-derived prefix into `persist(...)`." The Protocol-level kwarg is also better dependency-inversion hygiene — the adapter takes what it's told rather than burying source-of-truth choices internally. Compromise: keep the kwarg (signal compliance + DIP); rename it honestly (`backup_ref_id_prefix`); fall back to the domain `generate_job_id()` when `session_id` is None (no semantic lie about what the value actually represents).

## Architectural constraints (re-verified)

- `git worktree` shares `refs/heads/*` with the bare repo. One `reset_hard` in the worktree moves the shared ref everywhere — no separate cache-ref reset. `git fetch` cannot update the checked-out branch ([git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree)).
- `job_id` is generated inside `git_worktree_provider.py:74` and never surfaces to `agent_service` — that's why the prefix is sourced from `session_id` (when set) with `generate_job_id()` fallback (always 32 hex chars, sliced to 8).
- `BackupBranchName.job_id_prefix` is `Field(min_length=8, max_length=8)`; the prefix string MUST be exactly 8 chars — `(session_id or generate_job_id())[:8]` guarantees this (both `session_id` and `generate_job_id()` output ≥8 chars).
- `BackupBranchName.is_backup()` checks for the literal `-backup-` infix; the merger's `cleanup_backup_branches` (`git_branch_merger.py:139-189`, invoked from `ralph_workflow.py:1056-1066` at workflow end) sweeps every ref matching the infix — the new ref flows through automatically.
- The replay SHA is observability-only — rides `commit_sha` on the iteration `ResultEvent`. The merger derives the feature tip from `origin/{feature_branch}` independently.

## Documentation consulted (official sources)

- `git commit-tree <tree> -p <parent> -m <message>` ([git-scm.com/docs/git-commit-tree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit-tree), [kernel.org](https://www.kernel.org/pub/software/scm/git/docs/git-commit-tree.html)) — correct primitive for creating a commit from an existing tree without working-tree manipulation.
- `<rev>^{tree}` peeling operator ([git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse)) — safe extraction of tree from any tree-ish (HEAD, full SHA, ref).
- `git worktree` semantics ([git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree)) — `refs/heads/*` is repository-scoped; one worktree reset moves the shared ref; same branch cannot be checked out twice.
- `importlib.metadata.version()` ([docs.python.org/3/library/importlib.metadata](https://docs.python.org/3/library/importlib.metadata.html)) — canonical Python 3.12 best practice; reads from installed wheel's dist-info. Per-call caching is NOT API-guaranteed; module-level assignment is the documented mitigation pattern.
- `uv run` auto-sync semantics ([Simon Willison's TIL on dependency groups](https://til.simonwillison.net/uv/dependency-groups), [pydevtools how-to](https://pydevtools.com/handbook/how-to/how-to-run-tests-using-uv/)) — `uv run pytest` installs the current project as editable in the venv before invocation, so `version("kodezart")` resolves under `make test`. Raw `pytest` does not.

## Out of scope (per ticket)

Merger consolidate / DIVERGENT / SOURCE_MISSING; backup-branch sweep logic; evaluator prompts/criteria/feature-tip derivation; new SSE event types; surfacing `job_id` from `git_worktree_provider` upward; `pyproject.toml` edits; `check_health()` body and `health.py` module docstring; `tests/api/v1/test_health.py` (literal `"0.1.0"` continues to pass); `stream_workflow`'s public signature; disabling any lint rule; adding `try/except PackageNotFoundError` fallback (per project's no-fallback rule).

## Anti-patterns (must NOT appear in the diff)

Resetting before pushing the backup; `--force` push; `read-tree`/`checkout-index`/`add -A`/`commit` working-tree reconstruction; separate bare-cache ref reset; replay SHA as canonical feature tip; backup ref without `-backup-` infix; `commit_tree` when trees are equal; `_APP_VERSION` literal of any value; `tomllib`/`open()` at module load; editing `health.py` module docstring or `check_health()` body; `assert remote_tip is not None` as a production guard; `import uuid` in `agent_service.py`; re-using divergent HEAD's message on the tree-equal branch.

requiredChanges.description:
Two changes:

(A) Extend `GitService` Protocol with three new async methods:

```python
async def reset_hard(self, cwd: str, ref: str) -> None:
    """Hard-reset working tree + index + HEAD to *ref*. Maps to ``git reset --hard <ref>``."""
    ...

async def tree_of(self, cwd: str, ref: str) -> str:
    """Tree SHA reachable from *ref*. Maps to ``git rev-parse <ref>^{tree}``."""
    ...

async def commit_tree(
    self,
    cwd: str,
    tree: str,
    parent: str,
    message: str,
    author_name: str,
    author_email: str,
) -> str:
    """Create a commit object referencing *tree* with one *parent* and *message*.
    Maps to ``git commit-tree <tree> -p <parent> -m <message>``. Returns the new commit SHA."""
    ...
```

(B) Extend `ChangePersister.persist` (lines 188-200) with `backup_ref_id_prefix: str` keyword-only param:

```python
@runtime_checkable
class ChangePersister(Protocol):
    """Detects changes, generates commit message, commits, pushes."""

    async def persist(
        self,
        *,
        workspace_path: str,
        branch: str,
        executor: AgentExecutor,
        backup_ref_id_prefix: str,
    ) -> PersistResult | None:
        """Commit and push changes. ``None`` if clean.

        ``backup_ref_id_prefix`` is an exactly-8-char identifier used to
        name a backup ref ``{branch}-backup-{prefix}`` if the persister
        needs to preserve a divergent local line during recovery.
        """
        ...
```
requiredChanges.rationale: Protocols are the single source of truth for cross-boundary contracts in this codebase (`CONTRIBUTING.md:74-87`). The prior draft updated the adapter but not the port — producing a visibly broken contract that the reviewer flagged. Updating the port forces `FakeChangePersister.persist` and every call site to align in this same PR.

requiredChanges.description:
Four changes (one DRY refactor + three new methods + one helper extension):

(A) Add a private static helper at the bottom of the class to deduplicate the author env dict:

```python
@staticmethod
def _author_env(name: str, email: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Build the GIT_{AUTHOR,COMMITTER}_{NAME,EMAIL} env dict for a git invocation."""
    return {
        "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": name,
        "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": name,
        "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": email,
        "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": email,
    }
```

(B) Refactor existing `commit` (lines 133-151) to call `self._author_env(author_name, author_email)` instead of the inline dict (only the `env=` literal changes).

(C) Extend `_run_output` (lines 318-329) to accept `env: dict[str, str] | None = None`; apply the same `process_env = {**os.environ, **env}` pattern that `_run` uses. Do NOT add a parallel helper — DRY violation.

(D) Add three new methods (each invokes exactly ONE git subprocess):

```python
async def reset_hard(self, cwd: str, ref: str) -> None:
    await self._run(["git", "reset", "--hard", ref], cwd=cwd)

async def tree_of(self, cwd: str, ref: str) -> str:
    return await self._run_output(
        ["git", "rev-parse", f"{ref}^{{tree}}"],
        cwd=cwd,
    )

async def commit_tree(
    self,
    cwd: str,
    tree: str,
    parent: str,
    message: str,
    author_name: str,
    author_email: str,
) -> str:
    return await self._run_output(
        ["git", "commit-tree", tree, "-p", parent, "-m", message],
        cwd=cwd,
        env=self._author_env(author_name, author_email),
    )
```
requiredChanges.rationale: Author identity must ride the replay commit (otherwise git falls back to `user.name`/`user.email` from system config — unpredictable in production); the same env dict is needed in `commit` and `commit_tree`, so extracting `_author_env` is the DRY fix (reviewer-driven). One subprocess per method matches the protocol contract and the existing adapter style. `rev-parse <ref>^{tree}` is the documented peeling operator for extracting a tree from any tree-ish ([git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse)). `commit-tree` is the correct primitive that avoids `core.fileMode` / `autocrlf` / symlink / gitlink / `.gitignore` drift ([git-scm.com/docs/git-commit-tree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit-tree)).

requiredChanges.description:
Add a third member to `PersistSource`:

```python
class PersistSource(StrEnum):
    WORKING_TREE_COMMIT = "working_tree_commit"
    AGENT_DIRECT_COMMIT = "agent_direct_commit"
    DIVERGENCE_REPLAY = "divergence_replay"
```

Also extend the `PersistResult` docstring to describe the new variant's `message` semantics:

> For `DIVERGENCE_REPLAY` tree-equal subcase, the message is the remote-tip commit's message (`commit_sha = remote_tip`). For `DIVERGENCE_REPLAY` tree-differ subcase, the message is the divergent HEAD's message, which IS the replay commit's own message (`commit_sha = replay_sha`).

No `match` statement on `PersistSource` exists in the codebase (verified) — adding the member is non-breaking.
requiredChanges.rationale: The recovery helper returns a `PersistResult` distinguishable from the other two paths externally. The docstring update locks in the message invariant: message ALWAYS describes `commit_sha`. This is the contract the prior draft violated on the tree-equal branch.

requiredChanges.description:
Five changes:

(A) Add import:
```python
from kodezart.types.domain.branch import BackupBranchName
```

(B) Replace module docstring (lines 1-11) with the EXACT text:
```python
"""Git change persister — ensures the canonical ref equals workspace HEAD.

Three persistence paths:
- Dirty working tree: generate commit message, stage, commit, push.
- Clean working tree, HEAD ahead of (or equal to) the remote tip:
  push HEAD's existing commit (no new commit).
- Clean working tree, HEAD diverged from the remote tip: push the
  divergent line to a backup ref on origin, reset the worktree to
  ``<remote>/<branch>``, and either skip the replay (when divergent
  tree == remote-tip tree) or synthesize one replay commit via
  ``git commit-tree`` whose parent IS the remote tip and push
  fast-forward.

Returns ``None`` only when HEAD already equals the remote tip.
Raises ``RuntimeError`` only when the pre-mutation backup push in the
divergence-recovery path fails — in that case no state has been
mutated (no reset, no commit-tree, no follow-up push).
"""
```

(C) Replace the `persist` method docstring (lines 51-60) with the EXACT text:
```python
"""Ensure ``<remote>/<branch>`` equals workspace HEAD.

Decision tree:
- dirty working tree → stage+commit+push, return ``PersistResult``;
- clean tree and HEAD == remote tip → ``None`` (no-op);
- clean tree and HEAD descends from remote tip (or remote is
  absent) → push, return ``PersistResult``;
- clean tree and HEAD diverged → recover (backup-push the divergent
  line, reset to the remote tip, skip-or-replay) and return a
  ``PersistResult`` with ``source = DIVERGENCE_REPLAY``.  Raises
  ``RuntimeError`` only if the pre-mutation backup push fails;
  no state is mutated in that case.
"""
```

(D) Add required keyword-only param to `persist`: `backup_ref_id_prefix: str`.

(E) Replace the divergence branch (lines 83-88) with:
```python
if not head_descends_from_remote:
    if remote_tip is None:
        msg = (
            f"Internal invariant violated: divergence branch entered "
            f"with no remote tip for {self._remote}/{branch}"
        )
        raise RuntimeError(msg)
    return await self._recover_from_divergence(
        workspace_path=workspace_path,
        branch=branch,
        head_sha=head_sha,
        remote_tip=remote_tip,
        backup_ref_id_prefix=backup_ref_id_prefix,
    )
```

(F) Add the helper (pinned signature, ordered body):
```python
async def _recover_from_divergence(
    self,
    *,
    workspace_path: str,
    branch: str,
    head_sha: str,
    remote_tip: str,
    backup_ref_id_prefix: str,
) -> PersistResult:
    backup_name = str(
        BackupBranchName(
            source_branch=branch,
            job_id_prefix=backup_ref_id_prefix,
        )
    )
    # Step 1: backup BEFORE any state mutation. Preserves the divergent
    # commit (and its tree) on the remote, independent of local GC.
    try:
        await self._git.push(workspace_path, backup_name)
    except Exception as exc:
        await self._log.aerror(
            "divergence_backup_push_failed",
            backup=backup_name,
            head_sha=head_sha,
            remote_tip=remote_tip,
            branch=branch,
            error=str(exc),
        )
        msg = (
            f"Workspace HEAD ({head_sha}) has diverged from "
            f"{self._remote}/{branch} ({remote_tip}); backup push to "
            f"{backup_name} failed — no state mutated"
        )
        raise RuntimeError(msg) from exc

    # Capture divergent-HEAD message + tree BEFORE reset (defensive: keeps
    # recovery correct even if a worktree pruned unreachable objects).
    head_message_divergent = await self._git.head_commit_message(workspace_path)
    head_tree = await self._git.tree_of(workspace_path, head_sha)

    # Step 2: single reset moves the shared refs/heads/<branch>.
    await self._git.reset_hard(workspace_path, remote_tip)

    # Step 3: tree-equality guard.
    remote_tip_tree = await self._git.tree_of(workspace_path, remote_tip)
    if head_tree == remote_tip_tree:
        # HEAD is now at remote_tip; head_commit_message reads remote_tip's
        # message — consistent with PersistResult.commit_sha = remote_tip.
        remote_tip_message = await self._git.head_commit_message(workspace_path)
        await self._log.ainfo(
            "divergence_recovered_tree_equal",
            backup=backup_name,
            commit_sha=remote_tip,
            branch=branch,
        )
        return PersistResult(
            commit_sha=remote_tip,
            branch=branch,
            message=remote_tip_message,
            source=PersistSource.DIVERGENCE_REPLAY,
        )

    # Step 4: replay as a single commit whose parent IS remote_tip.
    replay_sha = await self._git.commit_tree(
        cwd=workspace_path,
        tree=head_tree,
        parent=remote_tip,
        message=head_message_divergent,
        author_name=self._committer_name,
        author_email=self._committer_email,
    )
    await self._git.reset_hard(workspace_path, replay_sha)
    await self._git.push(workspace_path, branch)  # fast-forward by construction
    await self._log.ainfo(
        "divergence_recovered_replay",
        backup=backup_name,
        commit_sha=replay_sha,
        branch=branch,
    )
    return PersistResult(
        commit_sha=replay_sha,
        branch=branch,
        message=head_message_divergent,
        source=PersistSource.DIVERGENCE_REPLAY,
    )
```

Structured-log emissions added (additive): `divergence_backup_push_failed`, `divergence_recovered_tree_equal`, `divergence_recovered_replay`.
requiredChanges.rationale: Backup-push-first preserves the divergent commit object (and its tree) on the remote, codifying the operational invariant the reviewer asked us to document. Capturing `head_tree` BEFORE the reset is belt-and-suspenders — it makes correctness independent of any local-GC behavior. Reading `head_commit_message` AFTER the reset on the tree-equal branch fixes the prior draft's `PersistResult.message`/`commit_sha` invariant violation (both now describe the same commit). `if remote_tip is None: raise` is a real production guard (`assert` would be stripped under `-O`). The single `reset_hard` exploits `refs/heads/*` being shared across the bare repo and its worktrees ([git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree)).

Two changes at the persist call site (line 183 inside `_run_in_workspace`):

(A) Add import (use the DOMAIN helper, NOT stdlib `uuid`):
```python

```

(B) Before the existing `await self._persister.persist(...)` call, compute the prefix and pass it as a kwarg:
```python
backup_ref_id_prefix = (session_id or generate_job_id())[:8]
persist_result = await self._persister.persist(
    workspace_path=workspace_path,
    branch=persist_branch,
```

`session_id` is already a parameter of `_run_in_workspace` (line 133). In the workflow path it is None per `ralph_loop.py:115-117` (intentional — ralph loop does not maintain cross-iteration session continuity), so the fallback fires and `generate_job_id()[:8]` produces a fresh 8-char prefix per iteration. Both branches of `or` yield strings of length ≥8, so `[:8]` always returns exactly 8 chars — satisfying `BackupBranchName.job_id_prefix`'s `min_length=8, max_length=8`.
requiredChanges.rationale: Services depend on the DOMAIN layer for ID generation per the project's hexagonal architecture (`README.md:184-188`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:74-87`) — importing stdlib `uuid` directly in `agent_service.py` would violate that layering. The kwarg is required by the ticket's success signals; the fallback path is required because `session_id` is genuinely None at this call site in production today.

The 'no I/O' promise refers to `check_health()`'s function body (which stays a pure attribute read); the module-level call runs once at import. `importlib.metadata` does NOT API-guarantee per-call caching, which is why we store the result on `_APP_VERSION` — the module-level assignment IS the mitigation pattern.

```python
async def _git_output(cmd: list[str], cwd: Path) -> str:
    proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        *cmd, cwd=str(cwd),
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    )
    stdout, _ = await proc.communicate()
    return stdout.decode()
```
